details:
AstroGuardian is an interactive, offline-first web application prototype designed to help astronauts monitor their health, understand physiological changes, and access educational guidance during space missions, especially when immediate medical support from Earth is limited.

The application allows astronauts to manually record daily measurements, including heart rate, body temperature, sleep duration, exercise time, and mood. These measurements are stored locally and presented through interactive dashboards and charts. AstroGuardian compares recent measurements with personal historical averages to identify noticeable changes and help astronauts understand their recorded health trends.

A key feature is ASTRA, a voice-enabled virtual assistant that responds to supported health-related questions, retrieves recorded measurements, and provides educational information about spaceflight health risks. The system also includes an interactive human body explorer, guided measurement instructions, daily check-in reminders, and wellness challenges to encourage consistent health monitoring.

AstroGuardian provides an Emergency Navigator, which demonstrates how crew members could access situation-specific guidance during incidents such as chest pain, collapse, or communication difficulties. It emphasizes seeking help from trained crew members and following approved mission procedures rather than attempting medical diagnosis.

The application also offers educational guidance for different environments, including the International Space Station, deep-space spacecraft, and lunar bases. Its offline-first architecture helps demonstrate how essential information could remain accessible when internet connectivity is unavailable.

Technologies Used: HTML, CSS, JavaScript, Chart.js, Web Speech API, browser localStorage, Service Workers, Visual Studio Code, Git, and GitHub. The current prototype uses manually entered fictional measurements and does not require specialized hardware or external medical sensors.

Creativity and Innovation: AstroGuardian combines health monitoring, personalized trend interpretation, voice interaction, interactive space-health education, emergency-training guidance, and mission-environment awareness within a single application. Instead of presenting raw measurements alone, it focuses on helping non-medically trained astronauts understand the information and access appropriate guidance.

Intended Impact: AstroGuardian demonstrates how accessible, easy-to-understand health software could support astronaut self-monitoring, health awareness, and preparedness for future long-duration space exploration missions.

The project was designed with accessibility, usability, offline availability, limited communication with Earth, astronaut autonomy, and medical safety in mind.
